A successful measurement of that timescale would constrain — or falsify — the priority given to the timeless information layer. The atlas keeps it dated so the 4 Sep OR ask is not a missed row.

If recoverability deformation and support-loss pruning exist before time or geometry, what object in that layer becomes the gravitational self-energy E that sets the objective-reduction timescale t = ħ/E? Does a successful lab measurement of that timescale constrain (or falsify) the priority you give the timeless information layer?
